subject: Error in t(partial) %*% vcov :  non-conformable arguments

messages.author: 54210f841827bd5f
messages.subject: Error in t(partial) %*% vcov :  non-conformable arguments
parts:
Greetings,

I am getting this error message (see subject/title of post) when I run the following code:

hn<-ds(data,key="hn",convert.units=.001,truncation=list(left=10,right=200),cutpoints = c(10,19,36,69,79,133,168),formula = ~as.factor(daytime)+size+as.factor(habitat))

From what I have read online this is caused by two matrices being of incompatible dimensions for multiplication. It only happened when I added in the habitat factor. I am wondering how I can fix this?

Thanks

Steve

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in t(partial) %*% vcov : non-conformable arguments

Hi Steve, hi listfolk,

This seems to happen when there are difficulties estimating the
variance-covariance matrix (or rather the Hessian) post-optimisation.
Sometimes one can get around this, otherwise I'd like to make our code
more robust to this failure... Could you send me your data/code off-list
(I will not redistribute it) and I'll take a look?

cheers,
--dave

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in t(partial) %*% vcov : non-conformable arguments
parts:
Hello listers,

Dave managed to work out a fix for this problem in the package. He told me that the issue is that when estimating so many parameters and with binned data, the Hessian (or rather the covariance matrix) for the detection function gets hard to estimate. In this case the failure to estimate the covariance matrix means that the abundance estimation procedure also fails.

The fix can be downloaded by following the instructions here : https://github.com/distancedevelopment/distance/#getting-distance

He also mentioned that when working with binned data it is best if less factors be used since binned data loses some of the information that the raw data would contain.

Hope this helps you all in the future
